messages:
Marta: Hey all — I'm opening a docs PR to update SOC2 wording around audit-log retention and add a compact SDK snippet for emitting structured audit events. Need legal to confirm the phrasing and the example before we merge. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/2378 :eyes:

Josh: pinging @Amira (legal) — small wording change could have compliance implications. cc @Samira for the snippet details :thumbsup:

Samira: PR is up. I moved the old free-text example into a migration note and added a new example file at docs/snippets/audit_event_example.md. Changed docs/security/audit-logs.md to reference it. PTAL: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/2378/files

Marta: key asks: (1) Should we say "default retention: 90 days" or "up to 90 days"? (2) Is it OK to show masked user IDs in our examples, or do we need to avoid even pseudonymization guidance? (3) Can we show a concrete SDK snippet (py + ts) that includes a retention hint field?

Amira (legal): Short answers: (1) prefer "default retention: 90 days" and call out that customers can configure longer retention via contract; avoid "up to" which is ambiguous. (2) Fine to show masking guidance, but add a note: "Do not include raw PII in examples." (3) SDK snippet is fine as long as it stays example-only and we don't prescribe a legal-safe pattern. Please add which systems are affected (logging, audit export).

Samira: pushed a first-pass snippet. Python example (keeps things minimal):

```python
from redwood.audit import AuditClient
client = AuditClient()
client.emit_event({
  "event_type": "model.invoke",
  "user_id": "user:xxxxxx",  # example masked id, do not send raw PII
  "timestamp": "2026-06-15T16:02:00Z",
  "details": {"model": "redwood-7b", "latency_ms": 120},
  "retention_seconds": 7776000  # 90 days in seconds
})
```

Kevin: nit: use `retention_seconds` instead of `retention_hint` — seconds is unambiguous in examples and matches the SDK we shipped in v0.12. Also add a tiny TS example for the JS folks.

Samira: done — added TS snippet too and updated the docs frontmatter to mention migration guidance for v0.12 -> v0.13 SDKs. Small diff: changed `retention_hint` -> `retention_seconds`, added a one-line migration note.

Amira (legal): wording tweak suggestion for the docs copy: replace "we retain audit logs for 90 days" with "default retention period for audit logs is 90 days; customers can change this via account settings or contract." Also add a short bullet under "Sensitive data" that says "Examples mask user identifiers; do not include raw PII in logs."

Marta: I updated the PR description with the 'default retention period' phrasing and added a "Sensitive data" callout in the example file. Also added a migration checklist entry for internal ops (notify SRE + CS).

Samira: pushed commit 5df3a9c. CI passed, link to deploy preview: https://deploy.preview.redwood-inference.com/preview/2378 (thanks @devops-bot)

compliance-bot: Reminder: update SOC2 evidence tracker if this doc change affects evidence package. See https://internal.redwood/evidence.

Josh: LGTM from docs side, small suggestion to add a quick checkbox list at top of the doc for "What changed / Why" — that'll help reviewers on the audit runbooks. :white_check_mark:

Marta: good call — added a checklist in the PR description. Also created a follow-up issue to author a retention exceptions matrix we can link from this page: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/issues/412

Samira: I'll hold the merge until Amira posts an ACK in the PR comments. @Amira (legal) — can you drop a single-line approval when ready?

Amira (legal): ACKed in PR comments with one small copy suggestion (applied). From legal side this is good to merge. :heavy_check_mark:

Samira: merging now. Thanks everyone — will watch deploy preview and open a short post-merge PR if any wording follow-ups come up.

Marta: thanks all!
